previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of ischemic systolic heart failure, coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure triggered by non-compliance with his furosemide for two weeks. He presented with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and increased pedal edema. In the hospital, he was treated with intravenous furosemide, leading to improved symptoms and a weight reduction to 137.8 kg. An echocardiogram showed improved ejection fraction of 35–40%. He had episodes of supraventricular tachycardia, prompting an increase in metoprolol and outpatient Holter monitoring. His lisinopril was held due to elevated creatinine, and he was transitioned from atorvastatin to simvastatin for financial reasons. GERD symptoms improved with omeprazole. He was discharged home on optimized medical therapy, compression stockings, and instructions for weight monitoring and follow-up.

# Shortness of breath: Mr. ___ has had ___ worsening 
orthopnea and dyspnea on exertion over the last several weeks. 
The etiology of these symptoms are most likely multifactorial 
with medication compliance, decompensated CHF, OSA, and recent 
diagnosed arrythmia contributing. On admission, patient had CXR 
notable for mild to moderate pulmonary edema, similar to CXR on 
admission earlier this month. ECG and trops were are baseline 
x2. His 02 saturation was 89% on RA, improving to 98% with 2L 
NC. Patient notes not taking all of his meds over last week due 
to finances and his systolic blood pressure was elevated to 
150-170 on admission. Physical exam notable for b/l basilar 
rales, elevated JVP, and bilateral pitting edema. He was 
diuresed with IV lasix with moderate improvement of symptoms. 
However, he continued to feel SOB and tachypneic and was 
tachycardic in 110-130 range, raising concern for PE. A CTA was 
negative. Mr. ___ continued to ___ sub-sternal chest pain 
and feeling SOB and was further diuresed and blood pressure 
aggresively managed. On the night of ___, he was bradycardic 
to 27bpm with acute shortness of breath. The bradycardic episode 
spontaneously resolved. Given his CHF, brady arrythmia, and body 
habitus, there appear to be several contributing factors to his 
shortness of breath at night. He is encouraged to follow up with 
his PCP for evaluation of sleep apnea and medication compliance 
was also discussed with need to maintain a low sodium diet. We 
have diuresed him with IV Lasix to a weight of 135.2kg on 
discharge. On discharge he is on PO torsemide 40mg daily. 

#Arrythmia: Mr. ___ was found to have stretches of sinus 
tachycardia and bradycardia on telemetry that sometimes, but not 
always coincided with his symptoms. Cardiology was consulted and 
recommended a EP study, at which time a bi-ventricular pacemaker 
and ICD were placed. The procedure was well tolerated and 
without complications. He recieved antibiotics for 72 hours for 
prophylaxis. He will follow up with his cardiologist as an 
outpatient. On discharge placed on metoprolol tartrate 75mg BID 
for cost considerations.

#Chest pain: During admission, Mr. ___ complained of ___, 
substernal, non-radiating chest pain. It is unclear the source 
of the pain given negative CTA, negative troponins and baseline 
ECG. Symptoms were non-positional and improved with morphine and 
nitroglycerin. Recent cath in ___ showed a 60% LCx 
lesion. He is instructed to continue his blood pressure 
medications and daily aspirin and follow up with his 
cardiologist for further evaluation. A trial of PPI during 
admission failed to redose pain or symptoms. At discharge this 
pain has resolved.

#CHF: Patient had CXR, BNP, and clinical findings consistent 
with decompensated heart failure on exam. He was diuresed during 
admission with improvement of JVP, edema, shortness of breath, 
and CXR. Unclear what led to decompensation but medicine 
compliance most likely contributing as patient was hypertensive 
on admission and blood pressure was well controlled on home 
regimen during admission. On discharge his weight is 135.2kg and 
his diuretic regimen is 40mg PO torsemide daily.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

It was a pleasure participating in your care. You were admitted 
for increasing shortness of breath and chest pain. We believe 
you were having an exacerbation of your heart failure and so 
gave you medicine to help you urinate out excess fluid.

While you were here, you had an episode of significantly 
decreased heart rate. During this episode, you reported feeling 
similar symptoms to the ones that brought you to the hosptial. 

To treat this very SLOW heart rhythm, we have implanted a 
pacemaker. Due to your underlying heart disease, we have chosen 
an implant that also comes with a defibrillator to shock you out 
of a dangerously FAST heart rate in case that happens.

Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.  Be sure to see your cardiologist tomorrow for 
follow ups and labs.

Please START METOPROLOL TARTRATE 75mg twice a day.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Short of breath, chest pain, CHF.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral views of the chest were provided.  There is mild
interstitial edema evidenced by peribronchovascular thickening and subtle
Kerley B lines.  No large pleural effusion is seen.  No overt pulmonary
alveolar edema.  Heart size is top normal.  Mediastinal contour is
unremarkable, though aorta is slightly unfolded.  No pneumothorax.  Bony
structures intact.

IMPRESSION:  Mild pulmonary interstitial edema.

HISTORY:  ___ male with tachycardia, chest pain, and shortness of
breath.

STUDY:  Chest CTA.  MDCT images were generated through the chest after the
uneventful IV administration of 100 cc of Omnipaque intravenous contrast in
the pulmonary arterial phase.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images as well
as right and left oblique maximum intensity projection images were also
generated.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS:  The visualized portion of the thyroid appears unremarkable.  There
is no axillary lymphadenopathy.  Scattered small mediastinal lymph nodes along
the right paratracheal station do not meet pathologic size criteria, as the
largest one measures 9 mm in its short axis (2:17).  The aorta is normal in
caliber without evidence of dissection.  The pulmonary arterial tree shows no
filling defect to the segmental level.  Clearance of more distal branches was
not possible due to suboptimal bolus timing.  There is no pericardial
effusion.  Assessment of fine detail of the lungs is limited due to motion
artifact.  Trace right pleural effusion is present.

The visualized portion of the upper abdomen shows a hyperdensity in anterior
horn of the spleen measuring 14 mm in diameter (2:87).  Incidental note is
made of a lateral healed rib fracture on the left (2:39).  Otherwise, the
visualized bones demonstrate no aggressive-appearing lytic or sclerotic
lesions.

IMPRESSION:  No acute PE; trace right pleural effusion.

HISTORY:  Lead placement.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, there are lower lung
volumes.  Continued enlargement of the cardiac silhouette with engorgement of
indistinct pulmonary vessels consistent with elevated pulmonary venous
pressure.

The pacemaker leads extend to the right atrium and region of the apex of the
right ventricle.  No acute focal pneumonia.

HISTORY:  Pacemaker device.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, there is little change in the
appearance of the dual-channel pacer with leads in the region of the right
atrium and apex of the left ventricle.  Continued enlargement of the cardiac
silhouette with possible mild elevation of pulmonary venous pressure.  No
acute focal pneumonia or pleural effusion.
